docs.title: Home
docs.text:
No queues. Just gains.

Documentation · PyPI · Releases

pysportbot books fitness classes at sports centres that use the Resasports booking software. You can use it from the command line or from Python, or let it book your weekly classes as soon as bookings open, e.g. from a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow. It can also send you the result on your phone.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install pysportbot

pysportbot needs Python 3.11 or newer. With uv, uvx pysportbot runs the command without installing anything.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
# Find the slug of your centre (no login needed)
pysportbot centres --search madrid

# Tell pysportbot who you are; you are prompted for your password unless SPORTBOT_PASSWORD is set
export SPORTBOT_EMAIL="you@example.com"
export SPORTBOT_CENTRE="your-centre-slug"

# See what's on, then book
pysportbot activities
pysportbot slots Yoga monday
pysportbot book Yoga "2026-01-12 18:00"

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
from pysportbot import SportBot

bot = SportBot()
bot.login("you@example.com", "your-password", "your-centre-slug")

for slot in bot.daily_slots("Yoga", "2026-01-12"):
    print(slot.start, f"{slot.inscribed}/{slot.capacity}")

bot.book("Yoga", "2026-01-12 18:00")

docs.title: Book every week, automatically
docs.text:
Describe your classes in a config.json:

{
    "booking_execution": "Friday 07:30",
    "classes": [
        {"activity": "Yoga", "class_day": "Monday", "class_time": "18:00"}
    ]
}

Then start the booking service, e.g. every Friday from GitHub Actions:

pysportbot run --config config.json

It waits until Friday 07:30 and then books Yoga on the following Monday at 18:00. If the booking window has not opened yet, it keeps trying for up to a minute. It exits with code 1 if a class could not be booked.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:

  • Notifications: booking results on your phone with ntfy
  • GitHub Actions: weekly bookings without a server
  • API reference

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Installing pysportbot also installs the pysportbot command, so you can explore your centre and book classes without writing any Python. With uv, uvx pysportbot <command> runs it without installing anything.

Command What it does pysportbot centres List the centres and their slugs. Needs no login. pysportbot activities List the activities of your centre. pysportbot slots ACTIVITY DAY List the slots of an activity on a day. pysportbot book ACTIVITY START Book the slot that starts at START. pysportbot cancel ACTIVITY START Cancel the booking of the slot that starts at START. pysportbot run --config FILE Run the booking service.

docs.title: Logging in
docs.text:
Every command except centres logs in. It reads your email and centre from --email and --centre, or from the SPORTBOT_EMAIL and SPORTBOT_CENTRE env vars:

export SPORTBOT_EMAIL="you@example.com"
export SPORTBOT_CENTRE="your-centre-slug"

The password comes from SPORTBOT_PASSWORD, or from a prompt when you run the command in a terminal.

Why is there no --password flag?

A password passed as a flag ends up in your shell history and in the process list, where other users can see it.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Find the slug of your centre
pysportbot centres --search madrid

# List the activities of your centre
pysportbot activities

# List the slots of an activity on a day
pysportbot slots Yoga monday

# Book or cancel the slot that starts at a given time
pysportbot book Yoga "2026-01-12 18:00"
pysportbot cancel Yoga "2026-01-12 18:00"

# Print JSON instead of a table, for scripts
pysportbot slots Yoga 2026-01-12 --json
  • DAY is a date YYYY-MM-DD, today, tomorrow, or a weekday name such as monday for its next occurrence. Today counts as the next occurrence.
  • START is the start time of the slot, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, in the time zone of the centre.
  • --json prints a JSON array instead of a table. It works with centres, activities and slots.

docs.title: Global options
docs.text:
These options go before or after the command:

Option Default Description --log-level LEVEL WARNING, or INFO for run DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL. The default only shows the result. --time-zone TZ Europe/Madrid The time zone of the centre. --version Print the version and exit.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success. 1 The operation failed, e.g. the slot is already booked. For run: at least one class was not booked, see How the service books. 2 Invalid arguments or configuration, or missing credentials. 130 Interrupted, e.g. with Ctrl+C.

Errors are printed without a traceback. Add --log-level DEBUG to see it.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Used by Description SPORTBOT_EMAIL all commands that log in Account email. --email takes precedence. SPORTBOT_PASSWORD all commands that log in Account password. Without it, you are prompted in a terminal. SPORTBOT_CENTRE all commands that log in Centre slug. --centre takes precedence. SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_URL run ntfy topic URL, see Notifications. SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_ON run always or failure. --notify-on takes precedence. SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_LANGUAGE run en, de, es, fr or it. NO_COLOR all commands Set to any non-empty value to disable colored logs. FORCE_COLOR all commands Set to any non-empty value to color logs even when stderr is not a terminal, e.g. in CI.

For run, the SPORTBOT_* env vars override the corresponding keys in the config file. Empty env vars are ignored.

and SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_LANGUAGE env vars override the config file.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
You can keep the booking service running on a server, but you don't need one: a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow can run it once a week for free.

Say you go to Yoga on Monday at 18:00, and bookings open on Friday at 07:30.

  1. Commit this config.json to a repository. It contains no credentials: 
    {
    "booking_execution": "Friday 07:30",
    "classes": [
        {"activity": "Yoga", "class_day": "Monday", "class_time": "18:00"}
    ]
}
  2. In the repository, go to Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions and add the secrets SPORTBOT_EMAIL, SPORTBOT_PASSWORD and SPORTBOT_CENTRE.
  3. Add the workflow below as .github/workflows/booking.yml. It starts every Friday at 07:00 Madrid time, so it's ready well before bookings open at 07:30.
name: Weekly Booking

on:
  # Runs at 07:00 Madrid time on Fridays, all year round
  # The timezone key accepts any IANA time zone and handles daylight saving time
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 7 * * 5'
      timezone: 'Europe/Madrid'

jobs:
  book:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.2

      - name: Run pysportbot
        env:
          SPORTBOT_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.SPORTBOT_EMAIL }}
          SPORTBOT_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.SPORTBOT_PASSWORD }}
          SPORTBOT_CENTRE: ${{ secrets.SPORTBOT_CENTRE }}
          # Optional, see Notifications
          SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_URL: ${{ secrets.SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_URL }}
          # GitHub Actions shows colored logs, but its output is not a terminal
          FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        run: |
          uvx pysportbot run --config config.json --booking-delay 1 --poll-interval 0.5 --poll-window 60

Start early

Scheduled runs often start several minutes late, so start the workflow at least 10 minutes before bookings open. The service waits until the execution time anyway.

docs.title: Finding out if a booking failed
docs.text:
If a class couldn't be booked, pysportbot run exits with code 1 and GitHub marks the run as failed. Depending on your GitHub notification settings, you then get an email, so you know to book the class yourself.

For a push notification on your phone instead, add your ntfy topic URL as the SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_URL secret, see Notifications. If the secret isn't set, notifications are simply off.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: The booking service can send a summary of each run to your phone with ntfy, a free push notification service that doesn't need an account.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Install the ntfy app from the App Store, Google Play or F-Droid.
  2. Pick a long, random topic name that nobody can guess, and subscribe to it in the app. For example, generate one with: 
    python -c "import secrets; print('pysportbot-' + secrets.token_urlsafe(12))"
  3. Set the topic URL: 
    export SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_URL="https://ntfy.sh/<your-topic>"

After each pysportbot run, you then get a notification like this:

pysportbot: 1/2 booked
✅ Yoga · Mon 2026-01-12 18:00 · booked (3 attempts)
❌ Spinning · Tue 2026-01-13 07:00 · full

Keep the topic URL secret

Anyone who knows the URL can read your notifications and send you fake ones, so treat it like a password. Set it with SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_URL rather than in a config file you commit. The service never logs it.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Config key Env var Option Values notify_url SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_URL ntfy topic URL. Notifications are off without it. notify_on SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_ON --notify-on always (default) or failure notify_language SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_LANGUAGE en (default), de, es, fr or it

The option takes precedence over the env var, and the env var over the config key.

docs.title: When
docs.text:
By default, you get a notification after every run. With failure, you only get one if a class wasn't booked or the run failed.

If a run fails before it gets to booking, e.g. because the login failed, the notification contains the error message. If the config file itself can't be loaded, the service can only send that error if the notification settings are in the SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_* env vars.

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
Notifications are in English by default. Set notify_language to de (German), es (Spanish), fr (French) or it (Italian) to change that. For example, with de:

pysportbot: 1/2 gebucht
✅ Yoga · Mo 12.01.2026 18:00 · gebucht (3 Versuche)

Error messages stay in English.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: pysportbot run --config config.json --dry-run sends a notification too, with [dry run] in front of the title.

docs.title: Self-hosted and protected topics
docs.text:
• Self-hosted ntfy: use the URL of the topic on your own server. It must use https://, except for localhost.
  • Protected topics: put the credentials in the URL. For an access token, use https://:<access-token>@ntfy.example.com/<topic> (with an empty username, ntfy treats the password as a token). For a username and password, use https://<username>:<password>@ntfy.example.com/<topic>.

docs.title: Limits and failures
docs.text:
• A notification holds up to 4,096 bytes. If the summary is longer, e.g. because you book many classes, it lists the classes that weren't booked first and ends with how many it left out.
  • If the notification can't be sent, the service logs a warning and carries on. The exit code doesn't change.
  • The service also warns if the URL answers, but not like an ntfy server would, e.g. with a login page.

docs.title: Python library
docs.text: Everything the command line does is available from Python through the SportBot class.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
from pysportbot import SportBot

# Times without a time zone are taken to be in time_zone, the time zone of the centre
bot = SportBot(log_level="INFO", time_zone="Europe/Madrid")

# Find your centre (no login needed)
for centre in bot.centres(search="madrid"):
    print(centre.slug, centre.name)

# Log in with your email, password and the slug of your centre
bot.login("you@example.com", "your-password", "your-centre-slug")

Creating a SportBot sends no requests. login() logs in to the centre and fetches its activities. It raises CentreNotFoundError if your account is not registered at the centre.

docs.title: Browse activities and slots
docs.text:
# List the activities of the centre
for activity in bot.activities():
    print(activity.name)

# List the slots of an activity on a day, given as a date or a "YYYY-MM-DD" string
for slot in bot.daily_slots("Yoga", "2026-01-12"):
    print(slot.start, f"{slot.inscribed}/{slot.capacity}", "full" if slot.is_full else f"{slot.available} left")

Centres, activities and slots are frozen dataclasses: Centre, Activity and Slot. Slot times are time zone aware datetime objects in the bot's time zone.

Prefer pandas?

Convert a list of models into a DataFrame with pd.DataFrame(map(dataclasses.asdict, slots)).

docs.title: Book and cancel
docs.text:
# Book the slot that starts at a given time
slot = bot.book("Yoga", "2026-01-12 18:00")

# Cancel it again
bot.cancel("Yoga", "2026-01-12 18:00")

The start time can be:

  • a "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" string, in the bot's time zone;
  • a naive datetime, in the bot's time zone;
  • a time zone aware datetime, in any time zone.

book() returns the booked slot as listed before the booking, so its inscribed count does not include your booking yet. Both methods raise an exception if they fail, see Error handling.

docs.title: Time-critical bookings
docs.text:
Popular classes fill up within seconds of the booking window opening. To book with a single request at that moment, find the slot ahead of time and book it later:

slot = bot.find_slot("Yoga", "2026-01-12 18:00")

# ... wait until the booking window opens ...

bot.ensure_logged_in()  # log in again if the session has expired
bot.book_slot(slot)

book_slot() does not check whether the slot is full, because its counts may be stale by then: the API decides. ensure_logged_in() costs one request while the session is still valid, and logs in again with the same credentials otherwise.

If you want to book your weekly classes this way, the booking service already does it for you, with polling and retries.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
All pysportbot errors derive from SportBotError, so you can react to specific failures by type:

import requests

from pysportbot import SlotAlreadyBookedError, SlotNotBookableYetError, SportBotError

try:
    bot.book("Yoga", "2026-01-12 18:00")
except SlotNotBookableYetError:
    ...  # the booking window has not opened yet, try again later
except SlotAlreadyBookedError:
    ...  # nothing to do
except SportBotError as e:
    ...  # any other pysportbot error
except requests.RequestException as e:
    ...  # network error, e.g. a timeout

All exception classes can be imported from pysportbot. See the exceptions reference for the full hierarchy.

Network errors and retries

Network failures such as timeouts are not wrapped: they propagate as requests.RequestException. A request that fails to connect is retried up to twice, but a request that may have reached the server, such as a booking that timed out, is never sent again automatically. If you retry a timed-out booking yourself and the first request did succeed, the retry raises SlotAlreadyBookedError.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
SportBot(log_level=...) prints color-coded logs to stderr, with timestamps in the bot's time zone. Change the level later with bot.set_log_level("DEBUG").

pysportbot only configures its own pysportbot logger and never touches the root logger, so it does not change how your application logs. Its messages are printed once by its own handler, even if your application also configures logging, e.g. with logging.basicConfig(). Without a SportBot instance, pysportbot stays silent unless you configure logging yourself.

If your application manages logging itself, e.g. to send logs to a central handler, pass SportBot(log_level=None). pysportbot then installs no handler, and its records propagate to your root logger's handlers at the levels you configure, e.g. via logging.getLogger("pysportbot").

Colors are used only when stderr is a terminal. Set NO_COLOR=1 to always disable them, or FORCE_COLOR=1 to enable them when the output is not a terminal, e.g. in CI logs.

docs.title: Booking service
docs.text:
The booking service books a list of weekly classes for you. You describe the classes in a config file, and the service logs in, waits until the booking window opens and books them all at once:

pysportbot run --config config.json

python -m pysportbot.service --config config.json still works too, and takes the same options.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
Your credentials don't need to be in the config file. Set them as env vars instead:

export SPORTBOT_EMAIL="you@example.com"
export SPORTBOT_PASSWORD="your-password"
export SPORTBOT_CENTRE="your-centre-slug"

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The config file is JSON or TOML, chosen by its suffix. There are two ways to run it.

docs.title: Book now
docs.text:
To book Yoga next Monday at 18:00 right away:

JSONTOML 
{
    "booking_execution": "now",
    "classes": [
        {"activity": "Yoga", "class_day": "Monday", "class_time": "18:00"}
    ]
}

booking_execution = "now"

[[classes]]
activity = "Yoga"
class_day = "Monday"
class_time = "18:00"

docs.title: Book at a set time
docs.text:
Most centres open bookings a few days before the class. To book Yoga on Monday at 18:00 and Spinning on Tuesday at 07:00 as soon as bookings open on Friday at 07:30:

JSONTOML 
{
    "booking_execution": "Friday 07:30",
    "classes": [
        {"activity": "Yoga", "class_day": "Monday", "class_time": "18:00"},
        {"activity": "Spinning", "class_day": "Tuesday", "class_time": "07:00"}
    ]
}

booking_execution = "Friday 07:30"

[[classes]]
activity = "Yoga"
class_day = "Monday"
class_time = "18:00"

[[classes]]
activity = "Spinning"
class_day = "Tuesday"
class_time = "07:00"

The service waits until the next Friday 07:30, then books each class on its next occurrence after that.

Classes are always in the future

A class on the same weekday as the booking is booked for the following week. With "booking_execution": "Friday 07:30", a class on Friday at 18:00 is booked for next Friday, not the same day.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Type Required Env var email string yes, in the file or the env SPORTBOT_EMAIL password string yes, in the file or the env SPORTBOT_PASSWORD centre string yes, in the file or the env SPORTBOT_CENTRE booking_execution "now" or "<weekday> <time>" no, defaults to "now" classes list of classes, each with activity (the name as listed by pysportbot activities; case and extra spaces are ignored), class_day (weekday) and class_time (time) yes, at least one notify_url ntfy topic URL, see Notifications no, notifications are off without it SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_URL notify_on "always" or "failure" no, defaults to "always" SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_ON notify_language "en", "de", "es", "fr" or "it" no, defaults to "en" SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_LANGUAGE
  • Env vars override the matching keys in the file. Empty env vars are ignored.
  • Weekdays are English day names or their 3-letter abbreviations, in any case, e.g. Monday or mon.
  • Times use the 24-hour format HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, e.g. 18:00. In TOML, unquoted times such as class_time = 18:00:00 work too.
  • Unknown keys are errors, so a typo such as center doesn't go unnoticed. The service reports all problems in the file at once and exits with code 2.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description --booking-delay SECONDS 0 Wait this long after the execution time before booking. --poll-interval SECONDS 0.5 Time between attempts while a slot is not bookable yet or not found. Must be positive. --poll-window SECONDS 60 How long to keep polling after booking starts. --retry-attempts N 3 Attempts per class for errors that may be temporary, such as network errors. Must be at least 1. --retry-delay SECONDS 5 Time to wait after such an error. --max-threads N no limit How many classes to book in parallel. --notify-on {always,failure} always When to send a notification. Overrides notify_on and SPORTBOT_NOTIFY_ON. --dry-run Do everything except send booking requests, see below. --time-zone TZ Europe/Madrid The time zone of the centre. --log-level LEVEL INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL.

Delays can be fractions of a second, e.g. --retry-delay 0.5, and must not be negative.

All classes are booked in parallel. With --max-threads, the remaining classes are booked as soon as a thread is free, in the order of the config file.

docs.title: Dry run
docs.text:
--dry-run logs in, waits until the execution time and checks that each slot exists and is neither full nor cancelled, but it doesn't send any booking requests. With "booking_execution": "now" it runs straight away, which makes it a quick way to check a new config file:

pysportbot run --config config.json --dry-run

A successful dry run doesn't guarantee the real booking, though: a slot can still fill up in the meantime.

docs.title: How the service books
docs.text:
Popular classes fill up within seconds of the booking window opening, so the service gets ready a minute early and then tries quickly at the opening time:

T-60 s     log in again if the session expired (retrying on failure), and look up each slot
T          book: one request per class, all classes at once
T…T+60 s   try again every 0.5 s while a slot is "not bookable yet"

Here T is the booking_execution time plus --booking-delay, and polling stops --poll-window seconds after T. Each class looks up its own slot, so one slow lookup doesn't hold up the others. If a slot can't be found at T-60 s, e.g. because the calendar isn't published yet, it is looked up again when booking. With "booking_execution": "now", the service books straight away.

What happens after a failed attempt depends on the error:

Error What happens Result Not bookable yet, not available, or slot not found Try again every --poll-interval seconds until --poll-window ends. Polls don't count as retry attempts. failed or not found once the window ends Network error, unexpected API response or unknown error code Try again after --retry-delay seconds, up to --retry-attempts attempts. failed after the last attempt Already booked Stop. This includes a booking that timed out but went through: the next attempt finds it already booked. already booked Full Send one booking request anyway, in case one of the places is already yours, then stop. full, or already booked

At the end, the service logs a summary with the status and number of attempts for each class. It exits with code 0 if every class is booked or already booked (or would be booked, in a dry run), and with code 1 otherwise. That way a failed booking is easy to spot, e.g. as a failed scheduled run in GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
Every exception that pysportbot raises derives from SportBotError, and all of them can be imported from pysportbot. Network errors are the one exception: they propagate as requests.RequestException.

SportBotError
├── APIError
├── AuthenticationError
├── NotLoggedInError
├── ConfigError
├── CentreNotFoundError
├── ActivityNotFoundError
├── SlotNotFoundError
├── BookingError
│   ├── SlotAlreadyBookedError
│   ├── SlotUnavailableError
│   ├── SlotNotBookableYetError
│   └── SlotFullError
└── CancellationError

docs.title: ensure_logged_in
docs.text:
ensure_logged_in() -> None

Re-login with the stored credentials if the current session is no longer valid.

Long-running programs can call this before time-critical requests, because the session may expire some time after login(). It costs one request when the session is still valid. Otherwise it logs in again with the email, password and centre of the last successful login(), which the bot keeps in memory for this purpose. A re-login keeps the activities fetched by login(), so it sends no activities request.

Raises:

Type Description NotLoggedInError

If login() has never succeeded.

AuthenticationError

If the re-login fails.

APIError

If fetching the activities fails, when an earlier login failed and a full login is needed.

docs.title: book_slot
docs.text:
book_slot(slot: Slot) -> Slot

Book a slot found earlier, e.g. by find_slot() or daily_slots(), with a single request.

Unlike book(), this does not look the slot up again, so it suits time-critical bookings where the slot is found ahead of time. It does not check whether the slot is full either, because its counts may be stale by now: the API decides.
